entry.title: India: Income-tax Act, 2025 replaces the 1961 Act from 1 April 2026
entry.summary: The Income-tax Act, 2025 applies to tax years starting from 1 April 2026 and completely replaces the old law. For individuals with business income whose accounts do not require audit, the return due date is 31 August of the year immediately following the relevant year, and…
entry.content:
In force, 1 Apr 2026

The Income-tax Act, 2025 applies to tax years starting from 1 April 2026 and completely replaces the old law. For individuals with business income whose accounts do not require audit, the return due date is 31 August of the year immediately following the relevant year, and revised returns may be filed by 31 March.

For the employer:

  • Update payroll and tax-filing calendars and references for tax years starting 1 April 2026.

Source: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries - India, Individual - Significant developments

For information only, not legal or tax advice.

entry.title: India: Four Labour Codes in force from 21 November 2025
entry.summary: The Code on Wages 2019, the Industrial Relations Code 2020, the Code on Social Security 2020 and the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code 2020 took effect on 21 November 2025. They introduce a standardised definition of wages and extend gratuity to fixed-term…
entry.content:
In force, 21 Nov 2025

The Code on Wages 2019, the Industrial Relations Code 2020, the Code on Social Security 2020 and the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code 2020 took effect on 21 November 2025. They introduce a standardised definition of wages and extend gratuity to fixed-term employees after one year of service (against five years for full-time employees).

For the employer:

  • Review salary structures and contracts against the new uniform definition of wages.
  • Provide gratuity to fixed-term employees who complete one year of service.
  • Watch for final central and state rules, which were yet to be notified.

Source: KPMG India - Implementation of labour codes: What changes and road ahead

For information only, not legal or tax advice.

entry.title: Indonesia: Government Regulation 49/2025 changes the minimum wage formula for 2026
entry.summary: Government Regulation No. 49 of 2025 replaced the previous wage-setting framework after a Constitutional Court decision. The alpha coefficient used in the formula now ranges between 0.5 and 0.9, compared with the previous cap of 0.3, and sectoral minimum wages have been…
entry.content:
In force, 2026 · Applies to 2026 wages

Government Regulation No. 49 of 2025 replaced the previous wage-setting framework after a Constitutional Court decision. The alpha coefficient used in the formula now ranges between 0.5 and 0.9, compared with the previous cap of 0.3, and sectoral minimum wages have been reintroduced in some regions.

For the employer:

  • Check the 2026 provincial (UMP) and regency/city (UMK) minimum wage decrees for each work location.
  • Check whether a sectoral minimum wage applies to your industry (for example construction, energy, high-tech manufacturing); it can exceed the standard UMP or UMK.

Source: RSM Indonesia - PP 49/2025 minimum wage regulation

For information only, not legal or tax advice.

entry.title: Kenya: Finance Act 2026: gratuity exemption limited to 31% of emoluments
entry.summary: From 1 July 2026, gratuity qualifies for tax exemption only if the contract of service is for at least three continuous years (or an extension of a three-year contract) and the gratuity does not exceed 31% of emoluments earned in that period.
entry.content:
In force, 1 Jul 2026

From 1 July 2026, gratuity qualifies for tax exemption only if the contract of service is for at least three continuous years (or an extension of a three-year contract) and the gratuity does not exceed 31% of emoluments earned in that period.

For the employer:

  • Confirm the contract runs at least three continuous years before treating gratuity as exempt in PAYE.
  • Tax any gratuity above 31% of emoluments for the contract period through PAYE.

Source: Kenya Revenue Authority - Finance Act 2026: what it means for you

For information only, not legal or tax advice.

entry.title: Pakistan: Federal civil-servant Basic Pay Scales 2026 and 7% ad-hoc relief allowance
entry.summary: This applies to federal government civil servants only and is not a private-sector payroll rule. By Office Memorandum dated 21 July 2026, the Ministry of Finance approved revised Basic Pay Scales and allowances effective 1 July 2026 for federal civil employees paid from civil…
entry.content:
In force, 1 Jul 2026

This applies to federal government civil servants only and is not a private-sector payroll rule. By Office Memorandum dated 21 July 2026, the Ministry of Finance approved revised Basic Pay Scales and allowances effective 1 July 2026 for federal civil employees paid from civil and defence estimates. BPS-2026 replaces BPS-2022 and merges the earlier ad-hoc relief allowances; a new Ad-hoc Relief Allowance-2026 of 7% of running basic pay applies from 1 July 2026 until further orders.

For the employer:

  • Federal payroll units: fix pay in BPS-2026 point to point from the stage held on 30 June 2026.
  • Stop the Ad-hoc Relief Allowances of 2022 (15%) and 2025 (10%), which cease on 1 July 2026, and pay the 7% allowance instead.
  • Annual increment remains admissible on 1 December each year.

Source: Government of Pakistan Ministry of Finance - Office Memorandum, Revision of Basic Pay Scales and Allowances of Civil Servants 2026

For information only, not legal or tax advice.

entry.title: Pakistan: New salaried-individual tax slabs with 35% top rate from Rs 7 million
entry.summary: The Finance Act 2026, enacted on 27 June 2026, reduced tax rates for salaried individuals in the First Schedule with effect from 1 July 2026. Income up to Rs 600,000 is untaxed, and the 35% rate now applies only to taxable income above Rs 7,000,000 (previously it applied from…
entry.content:
In force, 1 Jul 2026

The Finance Act 2026, enacted on 27 June 2026, reduced tax rates for salaried individuals in the First Schedule with effect from 1 July 2026. Income up to Rs 600,000 is untaxed, and the 35% rate now applies only to taxable income above Rs 7,000,000 (previously it applied from Rs 4,100,000).

For the employer:

  • Update salary withholding (section 149) to the new slabs: 1% over Rs 600,000; Rs 6,000 + 11% over Rs 1,200,000; Rs 116,000 + 20% over Rs 2,200,000; Rs 316,000 + 25% over Rs 3,200,000; Rs 541,000 + 29% over Rs 4,100,000; Rs 976,000 + 32% over Rs 5,600,000; Rs 1,424,000 + 35% over Rs 7,000,000.

Source: KPMG Taseer Hadi & Co. - A Brief of Finance Act, 2026 (July 2026)

For information only, not legal or tax advice.

entry.content:

entry.title: Bulgaria: Maximum insurable income rises to EUR 2,300; civil servants pay own contributions
entry.summary: Under the 2026 State Social Insurance Budget Act, the maximum insurable income rose to EUR 2,300 and the minimum insurable income for self-employed persons to EUR 620.20 from 1 August 2026. From the same date, civil servants under the Civil Servants Act and employees under the…
entry.content:
In force, 1 Aug 2026

Under the 2026 State Social Insurance Budget Act, the maximum insurable income rose to EUR 2,300 and the minimum insurable income for self-employed persons to EUR 620.20 from 1 August 2026. From the same date, civil servants under the Civil Servants Act and employees under the Judiciary Act pay personal social security contributions under an 80:20 employer-to-employee ratio, changing to 60:40 from 1 January 2027.

For the employer:

  • Apply the EUR 2,300 maximum insurable income from the August 2026 payroll.
  • Public-sector employers: withhold the employee share for civil servants and judiciary staff (80:20 in 2026, 60:40 from 2027).

Source: BTA - Social Security Income Thresholds Increase from August 1

For information only, not legal or tax advice.

In force, 1 Jul 2026

Ley 2466 de 2025 (Article 179) raises the surcharge for work on Sundays and holidays to 100% in stages.

For the employer:

  • 80% from 1 July 2025.
  • 90% from 1 July 2026.
  • Full 100% from 1 July 2027.

Source: Alcaldía de Bogotá (Régimen Legal) - Ley 2466 de 2025

entry.title: Czech Republic: Wages can no longer be paid partly in benefits such as vouchers

entry.content:
In force, 2026

For the employer:

  • Restructure any pay package that counted vouchers or benefit points toward the wage itself.

Source: JenPráce - Pracovní trh 2026

entry.title: Estonia: Pay Transparency Directive - recruitment rules being transposed, reporting postponed
entry.summary: Estonia is transposing the directive's recruitment-related rules: pay or a pay range must be disclosed before the job interview, candidates may not be asked about previous pay, and employers may not prevent employees from discussing their pay. The more demanding obligations -…
entry.content:
Draft — not yet law · Upcoming - transposition in progress

Estonia is transposing the directive's recruitment-related rules: pay or a pay range must be disclosed before the job interview, candidates may not be asked about previous pay, and employers may not prevent employees from discussing their pay. The more demanding obligations - structured pay systems and regular reporting by larger employers - are being delayed while Estonia seeks simplification.

For the employer:

  • State pay or a pay range in recruitment before interviews and remove salary-history questions.

Source: Majandus- ja Kommunikatsiooniministeerium - KKK: palkade läbipaistvuse direktiiv

For information only, not legal or tax advice.

entry.title: India: New tax regime slabs revised; full rebate up to INR 12 lakh
entry.summary: Under the alternate (new) personal tax regime, income up to INR 400,000 is taxed at 0%, rising through 5%, 10%, 15%, 20% and 25% bands to 30% above INR 2,400,000, and residents with total income not exceeding INR 1,200,000 receive a rebate of the lower of the tax or INR 60,000.
entry.content:
In force, 1 Apr 2025 · FY 2025-26

Under the alternate (new) personal tax regime, income up to INR 400,000 is taxed at 0%, rising through 5%, 10%, 15%, 20% and 25% bands to 30% above INR 2,400,000, and residents with total income not exceeding INR 1,200,000 receive a rebate of the lower of the tax or INR 60,000.

For the employer:

  • Compute TDS on salary for employees in the new regime using the revised slabs and the INR 60,000 rebate.

Source: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries - India, Individual - Taxes on personal income

For information only, not legal or tax advice.

entry.title: Indonesia: Government-borne PPh 21 (DTP) extended to 2026 for employees earning up to IDR 10 million a month
entry.summary: PMK-105, applicable from 31 December 2025, extends the Article 21 income tax borne by government (PPh 21 DTP) facility, first set by PMK-10 of 4 February 2025, to the January-December 2026 tax periods for employees in the footwear, textile and apparel, furniture, leather goods…
entry.content:
In force, Jan 2026

PMK-105, applicable from 31 December 2025, extends the Article 21 income tax borne by government (PPh 21 DTP) facility, first set by PMK-10 of 4 February 2025, to the January-December 2026 tax periods for employees in the footwear, textile and apparel, furniture, leather goods and tourism sectors.

For the employer:

  • Check the entity's KLU code registered in Coretax falls within an eligible sector.
  • Apply the facility to permanent employees with fixed and regular gross income not exceeding IDR 10 million per month, and non-permanent employees up to IDR 500,000 per day or IDR 10 million per month.
  • Pay the PPh 21 DTP amount in cash to the employee at the time of salary payment.

Source: RSM Indonesia - Client Alert 21 January 2026

For information only, not legal or tax advice.
